rules.UserImpactDescription: Reviewers confirm access regularly; users without a confirmation lose it.

References.Title: Create an access review of an access package
Change lifecycle settings of an access package

rules.Title: Owner of a privileged workload identity
rules.CheckTitle: Service principals and applications with Control or Management Plane access have no owners.
rules.Description: A service principal or application with Control or Management Plane access has owners. Owners can add credentials and act as the workload identity at any time, without a directory role, PIM activation or approval: standing access to its privileges. Service principals of Microsoft first-party applications are not reported. Delegated permissions do not count as access of the object: the application acts within the rights of the signed-in user (EO.5005 reports delegated Control Plane permissions).
rules.Remediation: Remove the owners. Manage the application with roles of its tier, for example Cloud Application Administrator scoped to the application and eligible in PIM, and restrict credentials with an app management policy.
rules.EffortDescription: Removing an owner is a single change.
rules.UserImpactDescription: Former owners lose self-service credential and configuration management and use a scoped, eligible role or CI/CD workflow instead.

References.Title: Assign owners of an enterprise application
Assign Microsoft Entra roles at different scopes
App management policies (credential restrictions)

rules.Title: Owner of a privileged group
rules.CheckTitle: Groups with Control or Management Plane access have no owners.
rules.Description: A group with Control or Management Plane access has owners. Owners can add members, including themselves, at any time without approval or PIM, and so grant the group's privileges.
rules.Remediation: Remove the owners, or make the ownership eligible in PIM for Groups with approval on activation.
rules.EffortDescription: Removing an owner is a single change.
rules.UserImpactDescription: Former owners use an eligible, approved ownership instead.

References.Title: Assign eligibility for a group in PIM for Groups
PIM for Groups
Manage groups in Microsoft Entra ID

rules.Title: Unconstrained Azure role assignment delegation
rules.CheckTitle: User Access Administrator and Role Based Access Control Administrator assignments are constrained by conditions.
rules.Description: An Azure assignment of User Access Administrator or Role Based Access Control Administrator has no condition. Its holder can assign any role, including Owner, to any principal at the scope, including itself, so it is effectively Owner of the scope. Members of a group with the assignment are not reported separately, nor are the service principals of Microsoft first-party applications (for example MS-PIM, which manages PIM for Azure resources). Tenant-owned system-assigned managed identities created by Microsoft services (for example DefenderCSPMSecurityOperator for Microsoft Defender for Cloud) are not Microsoft first-party applications and are reported when their assignment has no condition.
rules.Remediation: Add a condition that constrains the delegation to the roles and principal types the holder needs to assign (under Conditions of the role assignment: 'Allow user to assign all roles except privileged administrator roles Owner, UAA, RBAC (Recommended)', 'Constrain roles', 'Constrain roles and principal types', 'Constrain roles and principals' or 'Allow all except specific roles'), or remove the assignment. Review Microsoft-managed system-assigned managed identities (such as DefenderCSPMSecurityOperator) and accept them as finding exceptions rather than modifying Microsoft-managed assignments without checking service impact.
rules.EffortDescription: Needs the roles and principals that the holder delegates.
rules.UserImpactDescription: The holder can only assign the roles and principals of the condition.

References.Title: Delegate Azure role assignment management with conditions
Delegate role assignment management with conditions (portal)

rules.Title: Control Plane access through nested groups
rules.CheckTitle: Control Plane access is not granted through nested groups.
rules.Description: Control Plane access is granted through a group that is a member of another group. Nesting hides who holds the access, and the owners and administrators of every group in the chain can change it. The export records the chain of groups of PIM for Groups memberships (eligible nested groups); the members of other groups are read transitively, so their nesting is not reported.
rules.Remediation: Grant the access through one role-assignable group with direct eligible members, or remove the nesting.
rules.EffortDescription: The members of the nested groups move to one group.
rules.UserImpactDescription: Members keep their access through the direct group.

References.Title: Use Microsoft Entra groups to manage role assignments
PIM for Groups
Best practices for Azure RBAC

rules.Title: Dynamic administrative unit with privileged members
rules.CheckTitle: Administrative units with privileged members have no dynamic membership.
rules.Description: An administrative unit with dynamic membership contains Control or Management Plane objects. Whoever can change the attributes of its membership rule (for example the user principal name) can add privileged objects to it or remove them, and so change which administrators manage them. Only users, groups and service principals of the Privileged EAM data count as privileged members: devices (for example the privileged access workstations of administrators in a dynamic device administrative unit) are not evaluated, because the data has neither the members of dynamic administrative units nor the administrative unit memberships of devices.
rules.Remediation: Use assigned membership for administrative units with privileged members, or make sure that only administrators of the members' tier can change the attributes of the membership rule.
rules.EffortDescription: Membership has to be maintained by assignment or a provisioning process.
rules.UserImpactDescription: No change for the members.

References.Title: Manage dynamic membership rules of administrative units
Restricted management administrative units

rules.Title: New Control Plane access
rules.CheckTitle: New Control Plane access since the previous snapshot should be investigated.
rules.Description: A role assignment classified as Control Plane exists in the newest Privileged EAM snapshot of the Privilege History, but not in the previous snapshot. PIM activations are not counted: they are temporary instances of eligible assignments. A role that was reclassified to Control Plane shows as new access. Both snapshots need objects with the role type of their assignments (Privilege History data of EntraOps 1.2.0 or later): the Privilege History keeps the objects of a limited number of snapshots. Delegated permissions are not counted here: EO.8003 reports new delegated Control and Management Plane permissions.
rules.Remediation: Check in the Privilege History and EAM Dashboard reports that the new Control Plane access was requested and approved, and remove it if not.
rules.EffortDescription: A review of each new assignment.
rules.UserImpactDescription: Only unexpected access is removed.

References.Title: View audit history for Microsoft Entra roles in PIM
Microsoft Entra audit logs

rules.Title: New tier breach since the previous snapshot
rules.CheckTitle: No new tier breach since the previous snapshot.
rules.Description: The newest Privileged EAM snapshot of the Privilege History has a tier breach that the previous snapshot does not have: a user or service principal holds a role assignment classified at a more privileged tier than the object. Tier breaches follow EO.1001 and EO.1003: Management and Workload Plane are both Tier 1, delegated permissions (EO.8003) and service principals of Microsoft first-party applications are not counted, and new breaches of unclassified objects (counted as User Access) are counted apart instead of being reported, as their tier is unknown (classify them, EO.2001). PIM activations are not counted: they are temporary instances of eligible assignments (as in EO.8001). Every new breach fails, also when others were removed and the number did not increase. The Privilege History chart counts every tier breach, including delegated permissions and Microsoft applications, so its number can be higher. A new breach can also come from a reclassified object or role. Both snapshots need objects with the role type of their assignments (Privilege History data of EntraOps 1.2.0 or later).
rules.Remediation:
1. Review the new tier breaches in the affected results, and in the Privilege History and Tier Breach Analyzer reports (EO.1001, EO.1003).
2. Remove the role assignments that are not needed, or move them to an account of the matching tier.
3. If the access is intended, reclassify the object to the tier of the role and protect it accordingly.
rules.EffortDescription: A review of the change between two snapshots.
rules.UserImpactDescription: Depends on the tier breaches that are removed.

References.Title: Enterprise access model
View audit history for Microsoft Entra roles in PIM
EntraOps classification and object tiers

rules.Title: New delegated privileged permission
rules.CheckTitle: New delegated Control or Management Plane permissions since the previous snapshot should be investigated.
rules.Description: A delegated permission classified as Control or Management Plane exists in the newest Privileged EAM snapshot of the Privilege History, but not in the previous snapshot, typically because an administrator or a user consented to it (the snapshots don't tell who; the audit log does), for example Directory.ReadWrite.All or Mail.Read for a new application. The application acts within the rights of the signed-in user, so it is no tier breach (EO.1001 to EO.1003, EO.8002), but whoever controls the application (its owners, credentials or redirect URIs) can obtain tokens of the users who sign in to it, and illicit consent grants are a common phishing technique. A new scope of an existing grant counts as new. Service principals of Microsoft first-party applications are not reported, except the Microsoft clients whose delegated permissions the tenant grants by consent (Microsoft Graph Command Line Tools, Graph Explorer, Microsoft Intune PowerShell, SharePoint Online Web Client Extensibility, Microsoft Developer Sample Data Packs, Azure AD Assessment and M365 Lighthouse API, as in EO.5005). Both snapshots need objects with the role type of their assignments (Privilege History data of EntraOps 1.2.0 or later).
rules.Remediation:
1. Find who consented and when in the Microsoft Entra audit logs (activity 'Consent to application').
2. If the permission is not needed, revoke it in Microsoft Entra admin center > Enterprise applications > the application > Permissions, or remove the delegated permission grant with Microsoft Graph PowerShell (Remove-MgOauth2PermissionGrant).
3. Restrict user consent to permissions classified as low impact from verified publishers, and use the admin consent workflow, so privileged permissions need an administrator's review.
rules.EffortDescription: A review of each new consent.
rules.UserImpactDescription: Users of the application consent again, or request admin consent, if a needed grant is revoked.

References.Title: Detect and remediate illicit consent grants
Configure how users consent to applications
Configure the admin consent workflow
